items.prompt: Which teeth are wide and flat for grinding food?

options.why: Incisors are at the front. They are sharp for cutting.
Canines are pointed for gripping and tearing.
Milk teeth are a child's first set of every type.

hints: These teeth are at the back of your mouth.
Feel them with your tongue. Are they sharp or flat?
Think about which teeth mash rice and vegetables.
items.explanation: Molars are wide, flat teeth at the back of the mouth. They grind and crush food.

items.prompt: Match each type of tooth to its job.
hints: Think about where each tooth is in your mouth.
Front teeth bite into an apple.
Pointed teeth next to them grip.
items.explanation: Incisors cut and bite, canines grip and tear, and molars grind and chew.

items.prompt: How many milk teeth does a child usually have?
hints: Milk teeth are a child's first set of teeth.
Adults usually have 32 teeth. Children have fewer.
Count the top and bottom teeth in a young child's smile.
items.explanation: A child usually has 20 milk teeth. They fall out and are replaced by up to 32 adult teeth.

items.prompt: How does sugar make a hole in a tooth? Put the steps in order.
items: Sugary food stays on the teeth.
Bacteria in the mouth feed on the sugar.
The acid slowly makes a hole in the enamel.
hints: It starts with food left behind.
Tiny living things feed on the sugar.
The hole comes last.
items.explanation: Bacteria feed on sugar left on teeth and make acid. The acid slowly dissolves the enamel and makes a hole.

items.prompt: How often should you brush your teeth?

options.text: twice a day, for about two minutes

options.why: Plaque builds up every day, so brush every day.
By the time teeth hurt, damage is already done.
Water does not harm teeth. Twice a day is enough.

hints: Dentists give the same advice to everyone.
Think about morning and bedtime.
How long is a good, careful brush?
items.explanation: Brush twice a day, in the morning and before bed, for about two minutes. Use toothpaste with fluoride.

items.prompt: A cow has wide, flat teeth at the back of its mouth. What does a cow mostly eat?

options.why: Meat eaters have sharp, pointed teeth for tearing.
A cow's teeth are made for grinding plants.
Cows do not catch fish.

hints: Flat teeth grind food.
Tough food needs lots of grinding.
What do cows eat in a field?
items.explanation: Cows eat grass and other plants. Their wide, flat teeth grind tough plants into small pieces.

items.prompt: A lion has long, sharp canine teeth. What does it use them for?

options.why: Flat teeth grind grass. Lions do not eat grass.
Lions dig with their paws, not their teeth.
Flat back teeth are better for crushing.

hints: Lions are hunters.
Pointed teeth are good at holding on.
What kind of food does a hunter eat?
items.explanation: Lions eat meat. Their long, sharp canines grip prey and tear meat.

items.prompt: The hard, white outer layer of a tooth is called ___.
hints: It is the hardest material in your body.
Acid can damage it.
The word starts with e.
items.explanation: Enamel is the hard outer layer of a tooth. It protects the softer parts inside.

items.prompt: Choose 3 habits that help keep teeth healthy.

options.text: brushing twice a day with fluoride toothpaste

options.why: Sugar left on teeth at night feeds bacteria.
This can chip or crack your teeth.

options.text: drinking water instead of sweet drinks

hints: Think about sugar and bacteria.
Cross out habits that leave sugar on teeth or could break them.
Look for habits a dentist would praise.
items.explanation: Brushing with fluoride toothpaste, dentist check-ups and choosing water all protect teeth. Sweets before bed and opening bottles with teeth harm them.

items.prompt: Sort the animals by the main kind of teeth they have.
hints: Think about what each animal eats.
Meat eaters need teeth for gripping and tearing.
Plant eaters need teeth for grinding.
items.explanation: Lions, sharks and cats eat meat, so they have sharp, pointed teeth. Cows, horses and elephants eat plants, so they have flat, grinding teeth.

items.prompt: Why do children's milk teeth fall out?

options.why: Brushing keeps teeth healthy. It does not make them fall out.
Bacteria can make holes, but that is not why milk teeth fall out.
The jaw grows bigger, which makes room for adult teeth.

options.text: Bigger adult teeth grow underneath and push them out.

hints: Children's jaws get bigger as they grow.
Bigger jaws need bigger teeth.
Where do the new teeth come from?
items.explanation: Adult teeth grow in the jaw under the milk teeth. As they grow, they push the milk teeth out and take their place.

items.prompt: Ika leaves an eggshell in vinegar for two days. The shell goes soft. What does this model show about teeth?

options.text: Acid can damage the hard outer layer of teeth.

options.why: The shell went soft, so vinegar did not make it stronger.
The eggshell is just a model. The acid did the damage.
Eggshell and enamel are both hard, but the shell is only a model.

hints: Vinegar is an acid.
The eggshell is a model for something hard on teeth.
What do bacteria make that harms teeth?
items.explanation: Vinegar is an acid, and it softened the hard eggshell. In the same way, acid made by bacteria can damage tooth enamel.
